verdict.rationale: pnpm is a Node.js-based CLI tool that runs identically wherever Node.js/its self-contained executable runs, and docs describe it as a drop-in npm replacement with consistent config (pnpm-workspace.yaml, catalogs, .npmrc-equivalent settings) and its own runtime management (installing Node.js itself), which implies cross-platform consistency by design, plus community reports of heavy real-world use in CI and various environments. However, no evidence explicitly confirms macOS/Linux/Windows parity, and one community report notes a past Windows/Electron-related symlink incompatibility issue, plus other complaints about symlinks getting messed up. missing for 10: explicit first-party statement of macOS/Linux/Windows support, dedicated Windows-specific testing/docs, and confirmation the symlink-based store works identically on Windows without caveats.
